en.title: Recording Shoot-Off Ties
en.excerpt: How scorekeepers record single-arrow sudden death shoot-offs and closest-to-center tie-breaker decisions.
en.content:
When Shoot-Offs Occur

In elimination match play, a shoot-off is triggered when an individual Recurve/Barebow match reaches a 5-5 set score, or when an individual Compound match concludes with identical cumulative point totals after 15 arrows.

Entering Shoot-Off Arrow Values

The Archeris mobile portal automatically transitions into Shoot-Off Mode. Each athlete shoots a single arrow within a 40-second time limit. The scorekeeper enters the single arrow value for each competitor.

The Closest to Center (CT) Decision

If both competitors score identical values (e.g., both shoot a 9 or both shoot a 10):

  • The line judge measures the distance from the arrow shaft to the exact center of the X-ring.
  • The scorekeeper taps the Closest to Center (CT) checkbox next to the winning athlete's score.

Match Winner Lock & Advancement

Once the shoot-off is submitted, the system declares the match winner, locks the scorecard, and advances the victor into the subsequent bracket round automatically.
